text:
neha: FYI incoming from customer (Acme) — p99 latency spike on streamed endpoint /v1/generate using model 'asteria-v1'. Started ~03:42 UTC after yesterday's onboarding. They see long tails and occasional ERR_STREAM_TIMEOUTs.
jamal: Can you paste the customer's request ID and a link to logs?
neha: Request id 0a7f3c, logs: <https://logs.redwood.internal/streams/0a7f3c|logs> — tail shows many rows like `tokenizer: slowpath encode 158ms` and streaming stalls around token 24000.
alex_r: Looking at the trace now. Root cause points to encoder slowpath for long multi-byte sequences combined with our new BPE merges. For very long inputs we go from O(n) fast path to O(n^2) steps in a fallback normalization. Sample from their payload (trimmed):
```
{"input": "...大量のテキスト... [~35k chars] ..."}
```
The tokenizer adaptation we pushed added extra Unicode normalization that triggers on certain CJK punctuation clusters.
sara_ml: Can repro locally with asteria-v1@canary and the sample. Repro script below:
```bash
python tools/repro_tokenize.py --model asteria-v1@canary --input tests/fixtures/acme_long_cjk.txt --log-level debug
# produces: tokenizer: step encode 142ms x 23000 tokens
```
jamal: Thanks. Two quick questions: 1) is encoding CPU-bound on the host or inside GPU process? 2) are we seeing KV-cache blowups later?
alex_r: CPU-bound inside model-worker process (affects streaming because encoder runs in main thread before forwarding chunks). KV-cache size normal, no blowups. Main issue is an expensive regex/normalization path.
neha: Customer impact: elevated p95->p99 from ~200ms to ~2.4s for long streams; some clients time out and reopen streams — causes duplicates. They've paused production traffic.
sara_ml: Immediate mitigations I can flip: revert tokenizer change for threaded encode path, or enable fast-bypass for >16k inputs to use legacy encoder. Which do we prefer?
jamal: Prioritize fastest customer relief: temporary pin to previous model revision and enable fast-bypass for long inputs. We'll follow up with a proper tokenizer patch.
neha: I've requested a rollback for Acme via console, pinned to `asteria-v1@rev-0b2`. Also applied a per-customer route override to set `tokenizer.fast_bypass=true` for requests > 16k chars.
```json
// route override example
{
  "match": {"customer_id": "acme"},
  "settings": {"model": "asteria-v1@rev-0b2", "tokenizer.fast_bypass": true, "batch.max_delay_ms": 4}
}
```
deploy-bot: deploy plan created: rollback asteria-v1 for customer acme -> canary rollback started (job id: rollback-3125).
ops-bot: @jamal @alex_r alert: cpu spike on worker-host-17 as we repro; isolating process and adding throttling.
jamal: Added a temporary rate-limit rule to prevent backlog: `rlimit.streams.per_customer=10` and bumped `streaming.idle_timeout_ms` to 4500 for Acme.
sara_ml: For the permanent fix: I'll remove the expensive normalization in the threaded path, add unit tests for CJK clusters, and add a tokenizer opcache for repeated Unicode segments. Planning a canary rollout next week.
neha: Customer accepted the rollback and is validating. They're asking for a mitigation playbook we can share.
ajex_r: (typo) alex_r: Adding playbook doc: <https://playbooks.redwood.internal/latency/stream-tokenizer|stream-tokenizer playbook> — includes repro steps, route override snippet, and rollback commands.
neha: Closing loop: Acme confirmed p99 back to baseline after rollback. Keeping this thread open for the follow-up patch rollout notes. :white_check_mark:
